subject: MSA / Order Form — ownership handoff & deployment controls
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acela.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: J. Patel <j.patel@acela.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: output & training boundaries

Tessa / Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. We're ready to move forward from a product perspective, but legal has flagged several items in the MSA and Order Form that we need clarified before Procurement can sign. High-level asks:

- Ownership: Acela needs a clear assignment of ownership over any Customer Output (definitions below) produced by Redwood’s hosted or dedicated deployments. We cannot accept language that gives Redwood rights to re-use or sell our outputs.
- Training / retraining: We need an explicit opt-out from using Acela data (including prompts, results, and feedback) to further train or fine-tune Redwood models. If opt-out is not available, we need a data escrow / notice process.
- Feedback license: Any feedback loop Redwood uses for product improvements must be restricted to an irrevocable, non-exclusive, non-identifiable aggregation license; no productization of customer outputs.
- Telemetry & retention: Please confirm telemetry retention windows and whether telemetry is accessible to third-party contractors.

I’ve attached a redline summary from Acela Legal (Acela_MSA_requests_v1.docx) and a marked Order Form. Can you route to your legal and product/privacy teams and give a single consolidated response to each bullet?

Requested timeline: Procurement aims to have counters by EOW (Thursday) to meet our internal go-live by mid-November. If any of these require exec sign-off, please call that out.

Appreciate a clear mapping: Acela ask -> Redwood position -> proposed clause text.

Regards,
Maria Gonzalez
Head of Vendor Programs — Acela Systems
Maria.Gonzalez@acela.com

---
Attachment: Acela_MSA_requests_v1.docx (docx, 92KB)
Attachment: OrderForm_20261029-draft.pdf (pdf, 48KB)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acela.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, J. Patel <j.patel@acela.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: output & training boundaries

Maria — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. I’ve looped in our legal lead (Irene) and Ben from commercial so we can respond with a consolidated proposal. Quick notes from my side so everyone is aligned before legal drafts language:

- We understand Acela’s priority is exclusive control over Customer Output in customer-facing productization. We generally support a narrow, customer-first definition of Output, but need to ensure operational telemetry and aggregated model metrics are retained for service reliability.
- Training opt-out: we can offer a firm opt-out for customer-provided records and prompts for hosted accounts (and an opt-in if customers want Redwood to use data for model improvements). For Dedicated/Private deployments we can guarantee zero-retention/training by default.
- Feedback license: from a product perspective, we prefer the ability to use anonymous, aggregated feedback to improve model quality. We can propose a clause that explicitly excludes commercial use of identifiable Customer Output.

Irene — can you propose redline language for: 1) definition of Customer Output, 2) a training opt-out clause that is enforceable for hosted accounts, and 3) a telemetry retention table (what we store, for how long, and who can access it)?

Ben — can you run the commercial tradeoffs (price delta / SLA impact) for offering a hosted training-opt-out add-on vs. including it in the base Order Form? Maria — if you have a preferred placement (Order Form checkbox vs. Order Form schedule), include that in your response.

Next steps: please aim to return a consolidated draft (redline) by Tue EOD so Acela Procurement has time to review. If any item needs exec sign-off, flag it here and I’ll escalate.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Tessa.Morgan@redwood.ai

---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acela.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, J. Patel <j.patel@acela.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form: output & training boundaries

Maria / Tessa — quick commercial perspective:

- Training opt-out (hosted): we can offer it as a paid add-on (one-time onboarding fee + 15% premium on hosted throughput pricing) or as a standard feature for accounts that commit to Dedicated capacity. The premium reflects the loss of model-improvement feedback and additional data isolation work.
- SLA / Prod implications: Opt-out customers will still receive standard SLAs but we will limit certain proactive model improvements that rely on customer telemetry. That should be documented in an SLA appendix.
- Timing: if Acela wants the opt-out in the Order Form as a checkbox, we can ship that UI + billing flag within two weeks after signature (needs product eng confirmation).

If Acela can accept the opt-out as a paid add-on, we likely avoid executive approval. If they insist on opt-out for free accounts, I’ll need to get a pricing exception approved.

Will follow up with a short pricing note and the delta ranges by COB.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acela.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, J. Patel <j.patel@acela.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: output & training boundaries

Maria — thanks for the redline and clear asks. I’ve prepared an initial set of redlines and commentary attached (Acela_MSA_requests_v1.docx). Summary of our proposed positions below — I’ll include exact clause text in the attachment but want to surface the high-level tradeoffs.

1) Definitions / Customer Output
- Proposal: Define "Customer Output" as: (a) text, image, code, or other content generated by the model in response to Customer input; and (b) derivative improvements created solely from that Customer Output. Exclude aggregated model metrics and anonymized statistics.
- Reasoning: provides Acela a clear ownership claim over end-user-facing outputs while preserving Redwood’s right to maintain and improve service performance using non-identifiable metrics.

2) Training / Retraining Opt-out
- Proposal: Offer an explicit opt-out mechanism in the Order Form where Customer may select "No use of Customer Data for model training or improvement." For hosted deployments, opt-out means: (i) we segregate and stop using Customer-provided prompts, responses, and labeled feedback for model training; (ii) we still retain operational logs for troubleshooting but will scope anonymization and retention (see telemetry below).
- Enforcement: Include audit rights limited to verification (hashed samples) and a monthly attestation. Dedicated and Private deployments: default no-use unless Customer expressly opts in.

3) Feedback License
- Proposal: Narrow license grant: Customer grants Redwood a perpetual, non-exclusive, worldwide license to use aggregated, de-identified feedback for the sole purpose of improving the Service. Explicitly exclude the right to re-sell or commercialize Customer Output or to train third-party models using identifiable Customer Output.

4) Telemetry & Retention
- Proposal: Telemetry categories and retention windows (high-level):
  - Request/response metadata (request id, timestamp, latency): 12 months
  - Error traces and service logs (stack traces, execution metrics): 18 months
  - Full request/response payloads for debugging: retained 30 days by default, 90 days if opt-in for extended support; can be disabled if opt-out selected and Dedicated is chosen.
  - Access: internal SOC & SRE teams; third-party contractors only under SOC2-aligned contracts and restricted-scoped SSO access.

Executive escalation: The training opt-out for hosted accounts is a commercial concession with price impact. Ben has proposed an add-on pricing structure; if Acela requests opt-out as a no-cost standard term, we will require VP-level sign-off.

Next steps:
- I will attach a redline of the MSA with proposed text for the three clauses above (see attached).
- Tessa / Ben: confirm whether you want the opt-out implemented as Order Form checkbox vs. Schedule (I recommend checkbox for clarity).
- Maria: can you confirm whether Acela requires the opt-out to cover any subcontractor/partner-hosted inference (i.e., cloud partners) or only Redwood-managed endpoints? That will affect our proposed language.

Thanks — I’ll be available for a quick call if needed this afternoon.

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai
